background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">Read Heavy&nbsp;</span></div><div><font size="3">Assume 100 : 1 (Read : Write)</font></div><div><font size="3">Assume 500M new URL per month&nbsp;</font></div><div><font size="3">with 100 : 1&nbsp;</font></div><div><font size="3">50B -&gt; Redirection in same period&nbsp;</font></div><div><font size="3">QPS = 500M /(30days * 24Hours*3600 seconds) ~ 200 URL/Sec</font></div><div><font size="3">Considering 100:1 =&gt; 100*200URL/Sec = 20K URL/Sec Redirection</font></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="153" width="504" x="379" y="658" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="p-asIFV21MIEWjqzHZch-7" parent="1" style="whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;align=left;" value="<div><font style="font-size: 14px;"><b><u>Storage Estimation</u></b></font></div><div><br></div><div><font size="3">Store URL for 5 Years&nbsp;</font></div><div><font size="3">500M new URLs / Month then&nbsp;</font></div><div><font size="3">500M * 5 years * 12 = 30B&nbsp;</font></div><div><font size="3">Each stored Object 500 bytes</font></div><div><font size="3">30B * 500byte = 15000GB=15 TB</font></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="140" width="265" x="947" y="658" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="p-asIFV21MIEWjqzHZch-8" parent="1" style="whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;align=left;" value="<div><font style="font-size: 14px;"><b><u>Bandwidth Estimate</u></b></font></div><div><font style="font-size: 14px;">&nbsp;</font></div><div><font style="" size="3">200URL/sec&nbsp;</font></div><div><font style="" size="3">Total incoming data = 200*500bytes = 100 KB/sec</font></div><div><font style="" size="3">For read request&nbsp;</font></div><div><font style="" size="3">100:1 =&gt; 100KB/sec *100 = 10MB/sec</font></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="125" width="373" x="1247" y="658" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="p-asIFV21MIEWjqzHZch-9" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;rounded=0;" value="<div><font style="color: rgb(255, 181, 112); font-size: 14px;">Not Covered</font></div><div><font style="color: rgb(255, 181, 112); font-size: 14px;">1) Analytics e.g. How many times redirection happened</font></div><div><font style="color: rgb(255, 181, 112); font-size: 14px;">2) Our Service should also be accessible through REST APIs</font></div><div><font style="color: rgb(255, 181, 112); font-size: 14px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; by other services&nbsp;</font></div><div><font style="color: rgb(255, 181, 112); font-size: 14px;">- Assum short URL consist of combination of Numbers and characters&nbsp;</font></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="62" width="481" x="1157" y="252" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="p-asIFV21MIEWjqzHZch-10" parent="1" style="whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;align=left;" value="<div><font style="font-size: 14px;"><b><u>Memory Estimate</u></b></font></div><div><font style="font-size: 14px;">&nbsp;</font></div><div><font size="3">Follow 80-20 rule means 20% of URL generate 80% of traffic&nbsp;</font></div><div><font size="3">20k URL/sec =&gt;&nbsp;</font></div><div><font size="3">20k * 3600 Seconds * 24 Hours = 1.7 B</font></div><div><font size="3">To Cache it&nbsp;</font></div><div><font size="3">&nbsp; &nbsp; 0.2 * 1.7B * 500B = 170 GB(It can be less because lot of duplicate URL)</font></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="534" x="379" y="827" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="p-asIFV21MIEWjqzHZch-11" parent="1" style="whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;" value="<div><i><font style="color: rgb(234, 107, 102);">High Level Estimate (500M new URL/month)</font></i></div><div><i><font style="color: rgb(234, 107, 102);">100:1 (read to write )</font></i></div><div><i><font style="color: rgb(234, 107, 102);">New URLs = 200URL/sec</font></i></div><div><i><font style="color: rgb(234, 107, 102);">URL redirection = 20K URL/sec</font></i></div><div><i><font style="color: rgb(234, 107, 102);">Incoming Data =&nbsp; 100KB/sec</font></i></div><div><i><font style="color: rgb(234, 107, 102);">Outgoing Data = 10MB/sec</font></i></div><div><i><font style="color: rgb(234, 107, 102);">Storage for 5 Years = 15 TB</font></i></div><div><i><font style="color: rgb(234, 107, 102);">Memory for cache = 170GB</font></i></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="131" width="283" x="1259" y="832" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="p-asIFV21MIEWjqzHZch-12" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;rounded=0;" value="<font style="font-size: 24px;">3. font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><font style="font-size: 14px;"><b>One thing worth discussing here is 301 redirect vs 302 redirect.</b></font></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><font style="font-size: 14px;"><b>301 redirect</b>. A 301 redirect shows that the requested URL is “permanently” moved to the</font></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><font style="font-size: 14px;">long URL. Since it is permanently redirected, the browser caches the response, and</font></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><font style="font-size: 14px;">subsequent requests for the same URL will not be sent to the URL shortening service.</font></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><font style="font-size: 14px;">Instead, requests are redirected to the long URL server directly.</font></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><font style="font-size: 14px;"><br></font></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><font style="font-size: 14px;"><b>302 redirect</b>. A 302 redirect means that the URL is “temporarily” moved to the long URL,</font></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><font style="font-size: 14px;">meaning that subsequent requests for the same URL will be sent to the URL shortening</font></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><font style="font-size: 14px;">service first. Then, they are redirected to the long URL server.</font></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><font style="font-size: 14px;"><br></font></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><font style="font-size: 14px;">Each redirection method has its pros and cons. If the priority is to reduce the server load,</font></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><font style="font-size: 14px;">using 301 redirect makes sense as only the first request of the same URL is sent to URL</font></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><font style="font-size: 14px;">shortening servers. However, if analytics is important, 302 redirect is a better choice as it can</font></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><font style="font-size: 14px;">track click rate and source of the click more easily.</font></p>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="242" width="667" x="1400" y="1311" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="p-asIFV21MIEWjqzHZch-54" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;rounded=0;" value="<font style="font-size: 24px;">6. style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;" value="<font style="font-size: 16px;">Method 3</font><div><font style="font-size: 16px;">Generating Keys Offline&nbsp;</font></div><div><font style=""><p class="p1" style="font-size: 16px; margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;">We can have a standalone Key Generation Service (KGS) that generates random seven letter strings&nbsp;<span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">beforehand and stores them in a database (let’s call it key-DB). Whenever we want to shorten a URL,</span></p><p class="p1" style="font-size: 16px; margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;">we will just take one of the already-generated keys and use it. This approach will make things quite&nbsp;<span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">simple and fast. Not only are we not encoding the URL, but we won’t have to worry about duplications&nbsp;</span><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">or collisions. KGS will make sure all the keys inserted into key-DB are unique</span></p><p class="p1" style="font-size: 16px; margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><b>Concurrency ? - </b>As soon as key is used it will marked in the DB to ensure it will not be used again</span></p><p class="p1" style="font-size: 16px; margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><b>How to solve when two sever try to read the same key&nbsp;</b></span></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><font style="font-size: 16px;">Servers can use KGS to read/mark keys in the database. KGS can use two tables to store keys: one for&nbsp;</font><span style="font-size: 16px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">keys that are not used yet, and one for all the used keys. As soon as KGS gives keys to one of the&nbsp;</span><span style="font-size: 16px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">servers, it can move them to the used keys table. KGS can always keep some keys in memory so that it&nbsp;</span><span style="font-size: 16px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">can quickly provide them whenever a server needs them.</span></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><font style="font-size: 16px;">For simplicity, as soon as KGS loads some keys in memory, it can move them to the used keys table.&nbsp;</font><span style="font-size: 16px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">This ensures each server gets unique keys. If KGS dies before assigning all the loaded keys to some&nbsp;</span><span style="font-size: 16px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">server, we will be wasting those keys–which is acceptable, due to large numbers of keys we have&nbsp;</span></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><font style="font-size: 16px;"><br></font></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><font style="font-size: 16px;">KGS also has to make sure not to give the same key to multiple servers. For that, it must synchronize&nbsp;</font><span style="font-size: 16px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">(or get a lock on) the data structure holding the keys before removing keys from it and giving them to a&nbsp;</span><span style="font-size: 16px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">server</span></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><b><font style="font-size: 16px;">What would be the key-DB size?</font></b></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><font style="font-size: 16px;">With 62^7 ~ 35.21B keys (1Byte - one alpha-numeric character)&nbsp;</font></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><font style="font-size: 16px;">7*(35.21B) ~ 246GB</font></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><font style="font-size: 16px;"><b>KGS a single point failure?</b></font></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><font style="font-size: 16px;">Yes, it is. To solve this, we can have a standby replica of KGS.</font><span style="font-size: 16px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">Whenever the primary server dies, the standby server can take over to generate and provide keys.</span></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><span style="font-size: 16px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><br></span></p></font></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="609" width="623.5" x="289.5" y="3505" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="p-asIFV21MIEWjqzHZch-122" parent="1" style="whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;rounded=0;" value="<p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><font style="font-size: 16px;"><b>Data Partitioning and Replication</b></font></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><font style="font-size: 16px;"></font></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;">To scale out our DB, we need to partition it so that it can store information about billions of URLs</p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;">- Range Based Partitioning: We can store the URL by there first letter of URL or HashKey</p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;">Problem with this approach is that it can lead up to unbalanced server&nbsp;</p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><br></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;">- Hash Based Partitioning :&nbsp;<span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">In hash-based partitioning, we apply a hash function on a key (e.g., short URL key or original URL) and use the hash value to decide which partition stores the data. For example, a hash function may map a key to a number between </span><strong data-start="391" data-end="400" style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">1–256</strong><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">, where each number represents a partition. This helps distribute data evenly and enables fast lookups, since the same key always maps to the same partition.</span></p><br><p data-start="559" data-end="802">However, uneven traffic or hot keys can still overload certain partitions. To handle this, <strong data-start="650" data-end="672">consistent hashing</strong> is used,</p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;"><b style=""><font style="font-size: 16px;">Load Balancer</font></b></p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;">We can add a Load balancing layer at three places in our system:</p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;">1. Between Clients and Application servers</p><p class="p1" style="margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;">2. p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;
p.font: 301 redirect. A 301 redirect shows that the requested URL is “permanently” moved to the

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;
p.font: long URL. Since it is permanently redirected, the browser caches the response, and

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;
p.font: subsequent requests for the same URL will not be sent to the URL shortening service.

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;
p.font: Instead, requests are redirected to the long URL server directly.

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;

p.font: 302 redirect. A 302 redirect means that the URL is “temporarily” moved to the long URL,

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;
p.font: meaning that subsequent requests for the same URL will be sent to the URL shortening

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;
p.font: service first. Then, they are redirected to the long URL server.

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;

margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;
p.font: Each redirection method has its pros and cons. If the priority is to reduce the server load,

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;
p.font: using 301 redirect makes sense as only the first request of the same URL is sent to URL

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;
p.font: shortening servers. However, if analytics is important, 302 redirect is a better choice as it can

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;
p.font: track click rate and source of the click more easily.

p.font: 1. longURL is the input.

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;
p.font: 2. The system checks if the longURL is in the database.

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;
p.font: 3. If it is, it means the longURL was converted to shortURL before. In this case, fetch the

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;
p.font: shortURL from the database and return it to the client.

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;
p.font: 4. If not, the longURL is new. A new unique ID (primary key) Is generated by the unique

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;
p.font: ID generator.

p.font: The flow of URL redirecting is summarized as follows:

p.font: 1. A user clicks a short URL link: https://tinyurl.com/zn9edcu

p.font: 4. If a shortURL is not in the cache, fetch the longURL from the database. If it is not in the

p.font: database, it is likely a user entered an invalid shortURL.

p.style: font-size: 16px; margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;

font.p: We can have a standalone Key Generation Service (KGS) that generates random seven letter strings beforehand and stores them in a database (let’s call it key-DB). Whenever we want to shorten a URL,

p.style: font-size: 16px; margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;

font.p: we will just take one of the already-generated keys and use it. This approach will make things quite simple and fast. Not only are we not encoding the URL, but we won’t have to worry about duplications or collisions. KGS will make sure all the keys inserted into key-DB are unique

p.style: font-size: 16px; margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;
p.span: Concurrency ? - As soon as key is used it will marked in the DB to ensure it will not be used again

p.style: font-size: 16px; margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;

span.b: How to solve when two sever try to read the same key

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;
p.font: Servers can use KGS to read/mark keys in the database. KGS can use two tables to store keys: one for

span.style: font-size: 16px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

p.span: keys that are not used yet, and one for all the used keys. As soon as KGS gives keys to one of the

span.style: font-size: 16px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

p.span: servers, it can move them to the used keys table. KGS can always keep some keys in memory so that it

span.style: font-size: 16px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

p.span: can quickly provide them whenever a server needs them.

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;
p.font: For simplicity, as soon as KGS loads some keys in memory, it can move them to the used keys table.

span.style: font-size: 16px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

p.span: This ensures each server gets unique keys. If KGS dies before assigning all the loaded keys to some

span.style: font-size: 16px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

p.span: server, we will be wasting those keys–which is acceptable, due to large numbers of keys we have

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;

margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;
p.font: KGS also has to make sure not to give the same key to multiple servers. For that, it must synchronize

span.style: font-size: 16px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

p.span: (or get a lock on) the data structure holding the keys before removing keys from it and giving them to a

span.style: font-size: 16px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;

b.font: What would be the key-DB size?

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;
p.font: With 62^7 ~ 35.21B keys (1Byte - one alpha-numeric character)

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;

margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;

margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;
p.font: Yes, it is. To solve this, we can have a standby replica of KGS.

span.style: font-size: 16px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

p.span: Whenever the primary server dies, the standby server can take over to generate and provide keys.

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;

span.style: font-size: 16px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;

margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;

div.p: To scale out our DB, we need to partition it so that it can store information about billions of URLs

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;

div.p: - Range Based Partitioning: We can store the URL by there first letter of URL or HashKey

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;

div.p: Problem with this approach is that it can lead up to unbalanced server

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;

margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;

div.p: - Hash Based Partitioning : In hash-based partitioning, we apply a hash function on a key (e.g., short URL key or original URL) and use the hash value to decide which partition stores the data. For example, a hash function may map a key to a number between 1–256, where each number represents a partition. This helps distribute data evenly and enables fast lookups, since the same key always maps to the same partition.
However, uneven traffic or hot keys can still overload certain partitions. To handle this, consistent hashing is used,

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;

margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;

div.p: We can add a Load balancing layer at three places in our system:

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;

margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;

div.p: 2. Between Application Servers and database servers

p.style: margin: 0px; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;
